headline: Backward bifurcation and dispersal diversity govern population persistence and extinction
label: Mechanistic Population Dynamics Models
summary: Recent preprints and a published model show that persistence and extinction hinge on explicit model structure beyond simple thresholds.
synthesis: The common thread is mechanistic modeling of how populations persist or go extinct as structural parameters vary. A host-pathogen model of black Sigatoka exhibits backward bifurcation, so persistence depends on parameters beyond a simple threshold, and sensitivity and stochastic analyses identify its persistence drivers. A spatial study uses a competitive-balance metric computed from abundance data to show that dispersal diversity lowers species vulnerability to local exclusion. A published microbial model contrasts generalist and specialist nutrient strategies under stochastic feast-famine supply, where growth-death trade-offs shape outcomes. What is new across these works is explicit linkage of model structure, stochasticity, and trade-offs to persistence outcomes rather than to a single threshold. The three items span plant pathology, spatial community ecology, and microbial resource dynamics, so the shared emphasis is methodological rather than system-specific.
